Drohiczyn Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Drohiczyn, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are recorded in Drohiczyn from the late 13th/early 14th century; by 1921, 814 Jews (41%) were mostly murdered at Treblinka in 1942. This cemetery, likely established in the 19th century and confirmed active by 1855, was enclosed with a wooden fence and mortuary by the early 20th century. The last burials likely occurred in 1945, following the murder of two people in Drohiczyn after liberation. Poland formally closed the cemetery in 1964; a 1981 government survey found no visible traces remaining. In 2017, local activist Lena Dragicka worked with the Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage to erect a Holocaust memorial.
